cigars.researchNote: The regular sizes are made by Aganorsa Leaf in Esteli. Store-exclusive sizes exist, including a 5 x 50 Robusto and a 4.5 x 56 Short Toro that was made at HVC's own factory.

cigars.about: HVC's annual limited edition, released each fall since 2015 and sold in boxes of 50. Each year's release comes in a single size that has not been repeated.
cigars.researchNote: The size changes every year and the blend varies, so check the year. 2024 (5 7/8 x 52) has a Mexican San Andres wrapper; the 2025 10th Anniversary (6 1/4 x 54) has an Ecuadorian Habano 92 wrapper. Both use Nicaraguan binder and filler and were made at HVC's own factory in Esteli.

cigars.factory: Agricola Ganadera Norteña S.A. (Aganorsa Leaf, formerly TABSA)
cigars.about: The original Illusione line from Dion Giolito, a Nicaraguan puro built on Aganorsa Criollo '98 and Corojo '99 under a Corojo wrapper. It launched in 2006 with coded size names like ~88~ and ~888~, and since the 2022 repackaging it is sold as Original Documents Corojo with plain size names.
cigars.researchNote: Details are for the Corojo, the original blend. The family also has Maduro (Mexican San Andrés wrapper), Habano (made at AJ Fernandez's San Lotano factory), Candela and Ultra versions. Illusione says medium to full; Famous Smoke and Neptune list full. First made at Raíces Cubanas in Honduras.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Raíces Cubanas S. de R.L.
cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro rolled in Honduras, introduced in 2009 as a lighter version of Illusione's ~eccj~ blend and named for the Champagne town because it was made to pair with Champagne. It stayed at Raíces Cubanas when the rest of Illusione moved to Nicaragua.
cigars.researchNote: Illusione only says the wrapper is Nicaraguan; retailers identify it as Corojo '99. Le Taureau, Le Matin, La Vie and L'Alpiniste are pressed. The 10th Anniversary d'Aosta and the San Andrés wrapped Epernay Tuonela (2025) are different blends.

cigars.factory: Agricola Ganadera Norteña S.A. (Aganorsa Leaf, formerly TABSA)
cigars.about: A single-size, value-priced Illusione: a 4 1/2 x 50 short robusto with Nicaraguan long filler under a Mexican San Andrés maduro wrapper. It came out in 2013 and is sold in cabinets of 50.
cigars.researchNote: One size only. A Rothchildes CT with an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper was added in 2016. Illusione gives no strength; Famous Smoke's spec says full while its own description says medium body, so strength is left blank.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (viso and seco only, no ligero)
cigars.factory: Agricola Ganadera Norteña S.A. (Aganorsa Leaf, formerly TABSA)
cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro whose name means smoke of love, launched in 2014 and blended from lower-priming Aganorsa tobaccos with no ligero. It is one of the milder Illusione lines, and the Juniperos lancero placed fifth on halfwheel's Top 25 of 2015.
cigars.researchNote: Illusione and halfwheel only call the wrapper Nicaraguan; Corojo '99 comes from Famous Smoke. Illusione says mild to medium, Famous Smoke lists mild and Neptune lists medium. halfwheel's lancero review described a medium-full flavor profile.

cigars.factory: Agricola Ganadera Norteña S.A. (Aganorsa Leaf, formerly TABSA)
cigars.about: Illusione's 10th anniversary cigar from 2016, a Nicaraguan puro made mostly of seco leaf from a single farm and kept in regular production. halfwheel named it its cigar of the year for 2016.
cigars.researchNote: Strength is disputed. Illusione calls it mild bodied and delicate, Famous Smoke lists medium, and halfwheel's review of the Churchill found full flavor and body with medium-plus strength. The original 5 1/2 x 52 size came out in 2016; the Gordo and Churchill followed in 2018.

cigars.about: Illusione's Criollo-forward sister to the original line, first released in 2008 and made entirely of Nicaraguan tobacco. The Marelas Supremas, with its 109-style cap and gold foil, is Dion Giolito's favorite size.
cigars.researchNote: Illusione's site lists the origin as Honduras, where it was first made at Raíces Cubanas. halfwheel reported it moved to TABSA in Nicaragua in 2016 and Famous Smoke lists Nicaragua, so the factory is left blank. halfwheel called the wrapper Criollo Rosado in 2013 and Corojo Rosado in 2016.

cigars.factory: Agricola Ganadera Norteña S.A. (Aganorsa Leaf, formerly TABSA)
cigars.about: Introduced in 2016 for Illusione's 10th anniversary year and named after Bordeaux's garage winemakers. It pairs Corojo viso and Criollo viso from a single Aganorsa farm with an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Illusione says medium to full; Famous Smoke's spec lists full.

cigars.factory: Agricola Ganadera Norteña S.A. (Aganorsa Leaf, formerly TABSA)
cigars.about: A cult brand with a peace-symbol band, created by Andrea Molinari in 2001 and bought by Illusione's Dion Giolito in 2017. Illusione relaunched it in 2018 with a new blend in the original sizes.
cigars.researchNote: The year is Illusione's relaunch. The original OneOff dates to 2001 and was made by Plasencia with a Honduran wrapper. Illusione reblended it with all Nicaraguan tobacco and gives no leaf details, though Neptune still lists a Honduran wrapper. OneOff +53 and Black and Tan are separate blends.

cigars.filler: Nicaragua (Criollo '98, Corojo '99, ligero from Estelí and Jalapa)
cigars.factory: Agricola Ganadera Norteña S.A. (Aganorsa Leaf, formerly TABSA)
cigars.about: A full-bodied Illusione line, a Nicaraguan puro with a dark Corojo wrapper and extra ligero. It grew out of the MKULTRA, a stronger take on the ~mk~ corona, and became a regular line in 2011.
cigars.researchNote: Folded into the Original Documents family in 2022. Sizes are from Illusione's current page; older boxes use OP No. names (No. 1, 3, 4, 8, 9 and MKULTRA) with different dimensions, so check the box. Made at Raíces Cubanas in Honduras until the move to Nicaragua.

cigars.factory: Agricola Ganadera Norteña S.A. (Aganorsa Leaf, formerly TABSA)
cigars.about: Singularé began in 2010 as Illusione's yearly limited edition, one size and a new blend each time. Since 2023 it has continued as Singularé Origen, a regular four-size Nicaraguan puro that Dion Giolito built from his favorite parts of the earlier releases.
cigars.researchNote: Blend, sizes and factory are for the current regular line, Singularé Origen. The dated releases from 2010 to 2019 were limited editions with different blends. Illusione gives no strength or leaf type; Neptune lists it as full, with a Corojo Cafe Rosado wrapper and spice, earth and coffee notes.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic, other Central American tobaccos
cigars.about: One of the two original blends in the Indian Motorcycle cigar line, made under license by Phil Zanghi's Debonaire House at the De Los Reyes factory. It debuted at the 2015 trade show with an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: The filler countries beyond the Dominican Republic were not named at launch; Famous Smoke and Neptune describe the filler as Nicaraguan. Neptune's listing calls the wrapper Ecuadorian Connecticut, which conflicts with halfwheel and Famous Smoke.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic, other Central American tobaccos
cigars.about: The Connecticut Broadleaf version of the Indian Motorcycle line, made under license by Phil Zanghi's Debonaire House at the De Los Reyes factory in the Dominican Republic. It launched alongside the Habano in 2015.
cigars.researchNote: The filler countries beyond the Dominican Republic were not named at launch; Neptune lists the filler as Nicaraguan. Neptune's spec says medium while its description calls the cigar full bodied.

cigars.about: The first Connecticut-wrapped Indian Motorcycle cigar, made by Phil Zanghi's Debonaire House at De Los Reyes. It was released in Canada in May 2019 and reached U.S. shops later that year.
The maduro version of Brick House, using the same Nicaraguan filler blend under a dark Brazilian Arapiraca wrapper. It is the strongest of the three Brick House blends.
cigars.researchNote: Started in 2012 as a single size, the Mighty Mighty Maduro, with more sizes added later.

cigars.about: The mild Brick House blend, named for its two Connecticut leaves: a shade-grown wrapper and a broadleaf binder over the Brick House Nicaraguan filler. It was the third Brick House blend to be released.
cigars.researchNote: Both the wrapper and the binder are grown in Connecticut, which is where the name comes from. The foot band reads only Connecticut.

cigars.about: A mild, box-pressed Nicaraguan cigar from J.C. Newman with an Ecuadorian shade wrapper, priced as an everyday smoke. The name comes from a 1905 Tampa brand that the company revived.
cigars.researchNote: This is the original blend, now sold as Perla del Mar Shade; Maduro and Corojo versions also exist. Box-pressed. At its 2012 launch the binder and filler came from Pueblo Nuevo, La Reina, Condega and Jalapa; the filler was changed to stronger aged Nicaraguan leaf in late 2020.

cigars.about: The maduro version of Perla del Mar, a box-pressed Nicaraguan cigar wrapped in Connecticut Broadleaf. It is medium in strength and sold at a value price.
cigars.researchNote: Box-pressed. Reblended with stronger aged Nicaraguan filler and new packaging in late 2020.

cigars.about: J.C. Newman's value-priced handmade cigar from Nicaragua, sold in bundles of 20. It has a Sumatra-seed sungrown wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls this blend Quorum Classic; Shade and Maduro versions also exist. Sold in bundles of 20, and in 2012 J.C. Newman called it the number one selling bundle cigar in the world. The maker lists the wrapper only as Sumatra Sungrown; retailers and an older press release place it in Ecuador.

cigars.about: The maduro version of J.C. Newman's bundled Quorum cigar, with a dark Sumatra-seed wrapper and a Connecticut Broadleaf binder over Nicaraguan filler. It is a value-priced everyday maduro.
cigars.researchNote: Sold in bundles. No source says where the Sumatra maduro wrapper is grown. The maker lists the strength as Medium but describes the cigar as full-bodied.

cigars.about: The fuller Diamond Crown, made by Arturo Fuente with a dark sungrown wrapper from Oliva Tobacco's El Bajo farm in Ecuador over Dominican binder and filler. It was introduced in 2002.
cigars.researchNote: Reblended slightly bolder with new bands and boxes in summer 2026; sizes and prices stayed the same. Maker rates it Medium to Full; Neptune lists Full, calls the wrapper Ecuadorian Sumatra and gives 2003 as the release year. The maker says it was created to mark the company's 105th anniversary.

cigars.filler: Caribbean and Central America (countries not itemized)
cigars.about: A medium-strength Diamond Crown line made by Arturo Fuente with an Ecuadorian Havana-seed wrapper. It was released in 2010 for J.C. Newman's 115th anniversary and is named after the company's founder.
cigars.researchNote: Caeser is spelled the way founder Julius Caeser Newman spelled his name. The maker lists the Robusto at 4 7/10 inches while retailers list 4 3/4, and Neptune lists the filler as Dominican. A 5 x 52 size called 1895 is sold only at Diamond Crown lounges.

cigars.about: The strongest Diamond Crown, made by Arturo Fuente with a dark Havana-seed wrapper grown in Connecticut over five-year-aged Dominican binder and filler. It reached stores in late 2016.
cigars.researchNote: The wrapper is grown in Connecticut, not the Dominican Republic. Reblended stronger with new packaging in 2022. The middle size is spelled Marquise by the maker and Marquis by halfwheel.

cigars.about: An all-American cigar hand rolled at J.C. Newman's El Reloj factory in Tampa, using only tobacco grown in Florida, Connecticut and Pennsylvania. Even the boxes, bands and molds are made in the United States.
cigars.researchNote: The maker dates the revival of this 1910 brand to 2016, but the cigar first shipped in May 2019. Maker lists the Torpedo at 6 1/4 inches; halfwheel and Cigar Dojo list 6 1/8. A tubed President (7 x 47) is sold only at the factory.

cigars.about: A medium-strength Cuesta-Rey blend made by Arturo Fuente for J.C. Newman, with a Sumatra-seed sungrown wrapper from Quevedo, Ecuador over Dominican tobacco. Cuesta-Rey is a Tampa brand founded in 1884 that the Newmans bought in 1958.
cigars.researchNote: Full name is Cuesta-Rey Centro Fino Sungrown. Cigar Aficionado dates the line to 2002 and named the Pyramid No. 9 its No. 4 cigar of 2025. The maker and Neptune rate it Medium; Cigar Aficionado calls it medium-full.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan cigar from J.C. Newman that is rolled without molds and bundled while still wet in a royal palm leaf, so each cigar comes out in its own irregular shape. The method copies how the factory manager's grandfather made cigars on a Cuban farm in the 1940s.
cigars.researchNote: Regular production, but the Toro is released only twice a year, so it is not always on shelves. Each cigar is aged a full year after rolling. The Robusto was added in August 2026. Boxes of 20 arrive still wrapped in the palm leaf.

cigars.about: A small-batch cigar hand rolled at J.C. Newman's El Reloj factory in Tampa, reviving an early 1900s Cuesta-Rey brand that was once the official cigar of King Alfonso XIII of Spain. Two rollers make about 150 a day.
cigars.researchNote: The original blend is now called Angel Cuesta Rosado; a Shade version with a Nicaraguan shade wrapper followed in 2025. Binder and filler are undisclosed; the maker says only that the tobaccos come from three continents. Maker rates it Medium, while halfwheel found it medium-full to full.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A full-strength Nicaraguan puro from Joya de Nicaragua, introduced in 2001 as a throwback to the powerful cigars the factory made in the 1970s. It is the brand's best known line and the base for the rest of the Antaño family.
cigars.researchNote: Renamed Antaño Original in 2024 with new packaging; the blend did not change. Many shops still list it as Antaño 1970.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: The strongest cigar in the Antaño family, a Nicaraguan puro with a dark, oily Corojo Oscuro wrapper. Joya de Nicaragua released it in 2007 and aims it at experienced smokers.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates its strength 6 out of 5, above the original Antaño.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: The Antaño blend finished with an Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade wrapper, released in 2019. It is noticeably stronger and spicier than most Connecticut cigars.
cigars.researchNote: Some retailers list it as Antaño Connecticut. The Robusto was halfwheel's 2019 Cigar of the Year. Neptune lists it as Medium; the maker and Famous say medium to full.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A more refined take on the original Antaño, made with fillers aged up to five years. Joya de Nicaragua released it in 2017.
cigars.researchNote: The maker lists the wrapper as Nicaraguan Habano Criollo; halfwheel lists Nicaraguan Corojo Oscuro. The maker rates strength 4 out of 5; Famous says Medium-Full and Neptune says Full.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.wrapperLeaf: Ecuadorian Connecticut with a Nicaraguan Habano Criollo tip
cigars.about: A mild to medium Joya de Nicaragua cigar known for its two wrappers: a light Ecuadorian Connecticut body with a darker Nicaraguan Criollo leaf at the head. It debuted in 2010 and was rebranded as Joya Cabinetta in 2016.
cigars.researchNote: Originally sold as Joya de Nicaragua Cabinetta Serie. The maker's product page lists the Churchill at 46 ring, but its 2016 relaunch announcement and halfwheel list 48.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: Joya de Nicaragua's first cigar, dating to the factory's start in 1968, and a mild smoke with an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper. The maker says it still uses the founders' blend and it is the company's best seller in Europe.
cigars.researchNote: Now sold as Clásico Original. Clásico Medio Siglo is a separate, fuller blend with a Nicaraguan Habano Criollo wrapper. U.S. availability has been limited to select retailers.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A box-pressed premium line that began as a 2013 limited edition for Joya de Nicaragua's 45th anniversary. The regular Reserva Especial version followed in 2015 and uses fillers aged in oak barrels, including five-year-old ligero.
cigars.researchNote: The 2013 Edición Limitada was a Nicaraguan puro; the regular Reserva Especial (2015) added a Dominican binder. The maker calls it medium to full; Famous and Neptune list it as Full. halfwheel says the barrels previously held rum.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: Joya de Nicaragua's top-tier cigar, released in 2018 for the company's 50th anniversary. It is made in small yearly batches from select aged tobaccos and sold in boxes of 10.
cigars.researchNote: The blend is confidential; the maker does not disclose wrapper, binder or filler. The maker rates strength 4 out of 5 with no word for it; Neptune lists most sizes as Medium. A 6 x 60 El Embargo is sold outside the U.S.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A medium-strength Nicaraguan puro released in 2014 as the first cigar in Joya de Nicaragua's modern Joya series. It was blended to be more approachable than the company's stronger Antaño lines.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: The follow-up to Joya Red, released in 2016, and the first Joya de Nicaragua cigar with a Mexican San Andrés wrapper. It is a medium-strength smoke with fuller flavor than the Red.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's product page lists the Nocturno at 50 ring, but its own launch release, halfwheel and Neptune all list 6 1/4 x 46.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A box-pressed cigar added to the Joya series in 2018, the company's 50th anniversary year. It pairs a dark Ecuadorian Habano wrapper with a Mexican San Andrés binder and Nicaraguan fillers.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates strength 3 out of 5 and Famous and Neptune list Medium, though Famous describes the body as medium to full.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: The fifth cigar in the Joya series, a Nicaraguan puro made by Joya de Nicaragua as an exclusive for the retailer Cigars International. It launched in November 2019.
cigars.researchNote: A Cigars International exclusive, not on the maker's own site. It is confirmed only as a Nicaraguan puro; the wrapper variety is not published. No maker or retailer strength was found; a Cigar Coop review rated it medium to full. Current availability could not be confirmed.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A Connecticut-wrapped cigar that Joya de Nicaragua originally made as a diplomatic gift for Nicaraguan ambassadors. It went on sale in 2019 as part of the company's top Obras Maestras series and is finished with a fantail cap.
cigars.researchNote: First handed out in 2018 as an event-only cigar called No. 1, which was halfwheel's top cigar that year; regular sales began in 2019. The blend is based on Clásico. A 5 1/2 x 42 L'Attaché is limited to select retailers.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Tabacos Joya de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: One of Joya de Nicaragua's original brands, a value-priced Nicaraguan puro positioned below Clásico. It returned at the end of 2010 after about two decades off the market and has mostly been sold outside the U.S.
cigars.researchNote: The maker now calls the original blend Rosalones Auténticos. Rosalones Reserva and Rosalones CT are separate blends and are the two that reached U.S. stores in 2026. The maker lists a Nicaraguan wrapper; halfwheel in 2022 described it as Ecuadorian Habano. Sizes are as printed on the maker's site, in whole inches.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Puros Aladino at Las Lomas Jamastran
cigars.about: The flagship of JRE Tobacco Co., a Honduran puro made entirely from Authentic Corojo grown on the Eiroa family farm in the Jamastran Valley. Julio Eiroa blended it as an old-fashioned cigar and it debuted in 2015.
cigars.researchNote: Launched simply as Aladino under CLE Cigar Co. before JRE Tobacco Co. was formed in 2016. The maker has said strength varies by size. Strength here is from Famous.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Puros Aladino at Las Lomas Jamastran
cigars.about: A stronger, small-batch version of the Aladino Corojo, made entirely from Honduran Corojo with higher-priming leaves from the Eiroa farms. It was introduced in 2018 as a single robusto and has since added sizes.
cigars.researchNote: Regular production but made in limited monthly quantities. The Figurado is a box-pressed torpedo. A 5 x 44 Corona No. 4 Limitado is a separate limited yearly release. Famous and Neptune list it as Full; halfwheel's review of the Toro found it closer to medium.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Puros Aladino at Las Lomas Jamastran
cigars.about: The maduro version of Aladino, with a Mexican San Andrés wrapper over Honduran Corojo binder and Honduran fillers from the Eiroa farms. It soft-launched in late 2017 as the first follow-up to the original Aladino.
cigars.researchNote: The Corona, Cazador, Robusto and Toro are box-pressed. Famous and Neptune both list it as Medium.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Puros Aladino at Las Lomas Jamastran
cigars.about: An all-Honduran Aladino that uses a Cameroon-seed wrapper grown by the Eiroa family in Honduras over Corojo binder and fillers. It launched in 2020.
cigars.researchNote: The wrapper is Cameroon seed grown in Honduras, not leaf from Africa. Famous and Neptune both list it as Medium.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Puros Aladino at Las Lomas Jamastran
cigars.about: JRE's Connecticut-wrapped Aladino, with an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper over Honduran binder and fillers from the Eiroa farms. It was released in 2019 as the company's first Connecticut cigar without a sweetened tip.
cigars.researchNote: Famous and Neptune list it as Mild; halfwheel's review found the strength closer to medium. Famous describes the binder as Authentic Corojo.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Puros Aladino at Las Lomas Jamastran
cigars.about: A value-priced Honduran brand from the Eiroa family, shown in 2015 alongside Aladino and Tatascan and named for the family tobacco farm. JRE reworked it in 2025 as a mixed-filler bundle cigar in a single toro size.
cigars.researchNote: The original was a long-filler cigar with a Honduran Habano wrapper, plus a Maduro version. It went on hiatus in 2022. The 2025 relaunch is mixed filler, 6 x 52 only, with either a Habano-seed (red band) or Connecticut-seed (blue band) Honduran wrapper.

cigars.factory: Fábrica de Puros Aladino at Las Lomas Jamastran
cigars.wrapperLeaf: Connecticut or Honduran Habano, depending on the version
cigars.about: A Honduran brand from JRE Tobacco Co. known for its sweetened cap, launched in 2015 with Aladino and Rancho Luna. It comes in Connecticut and Habano versions.
cigars.researchNote: Two blends share the name: Tatascan Connecticut and Tatascan Habano, both with a sweetened tip. halfwheel calls the Connecticut wrapper Honduran; Famous and Neptune list Ecuadorian. Famous lists both blends as Medium; Neptune lists the Habano as Mild. Tatascan Yellow is a separate unsweetened bundle cigar.

cigars.about: Kristoff's Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapped blend over a Brazilian binder, introduced at the 2009 trade show. It is made in the Dominican Republic with the brand's pigtail cap and closed foot.
cigars.researchNote: Kristoff scores strength 3 out of 5 (medium) and Neptune agrees; Holt's and Famous list medium-full.

cigars.about: One of Kristoff's first lines, using a dark Brazilian maduro wrapper over Dominican and Nicaraguan tobacco. Rolled in the Dominican Republic with a pigtail cap and shaggy foot.
cigars.researchNote: Kristoff calls this line Original Maduro. Famous lists the wrapper as Brazilian Arapiraca and rates it medium-full; Kristoff (3 out of 5), Neptune and Holt's say medium.

cigars.about: Kristoff's milder blend, released in 2016 with an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper over a Nicaraguan binder and four Dominican filler leaves. Glen Case describes it as mild to medium in strength but big on flavor.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune lists it as mild; Holt's and Kristoff (2 out of 5) put it at mild to medium.

cigars.about: A Mexican San Andrés wrapped Kristoff that debuted at the 2015 trade show, with an Ecuadorian Habano binder and Nicaraguan filler. It is made in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: Kristoff scores strength 3 out of 5 but calls the cigar medium-full bodied. Neptune's table says medium; Holt's and Famous say medium-full. A 6 1/4 x 54 box-pressed toro was added in 2020 as a TAA exclusive.

cigars.about: A 2016 Kristoff release built around Brazilian tobacco, with a Brazilian Habano wrapper and Brazilian Sumatra-seed binder. It is a medium strength cigar made in the Dominican Republic.
Kristoff's Cameroon wrapped line, launched in 2015 with a wrapper the company says is aged seven years. A short 4 x 48 figurado was added in 2022.
cigars.researchNote: Kristoff scores strength 3 out of 5 and Neptune and Famous list medium; Holt's lists medium-full. Kristoff calls it medium-full bodied. Kristoff and Neptune list the Figurado as 4 x 48, halfwheel as 4 x 49.

cigars.about: A strong Brazilian maduro blend released in 2011 and named for Kristoff founder Glen Case. It is made in the Dominican Republic with the brand's pigtail cap and shaggy foot.
cigars.researchNote: Kristoff scores strength 4 out of 5; Neptune, Holt's and Famous all call it full. Kristoff, Neptune and Famous list a Honduran binder; Blind Man's Puff lists Dominican.

cigars.about: A full strength Kristoff line released in July 2016 with a Mexican San Andrés wrapper and Indonesian binder. Glen Case called it the strongest cigar the company had made, and the name is a customer's suggestion with the spelling changed.
cigars.researchNote: Halfwheel's 2026 report lists the filler as Nicaraguan and Pennsylvania broadleaf; earlier listings say Nicaraguan only. A milder Connecticut wrapped version, Mildly Pistoff Kristoff, was announced in 2026.

cigars.about: A 2019 Kristoff line with a Connecticut-seed shade wrapper grown in Honduras over Dominican and Nicaraguan tobacco. It smokes earthier and fuller than a typical Connecticut shade cigar.
cigars.researchNote: Kristoff scores strength 3 out of 5 but describes it as mild to medium bodied; Neptune lists medium, Holt's medium-full. Halfwheel reports that retailers describe this as the former Brittania Reserva under a new name; Kristoff did not confirm it.

cigars.about: An early Kristoff name that Glen Case brought back in 2018 with a new blend, the brand's first with a Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper. It launched through TAA retailers before going to all stores.
cigars.researchNote: 2018 is the relaunch year. The original Vengeance had a Brazilian maduro wrapper and was gone by about 2011. Kristoff lists the Perfecto as 6 1/4 x 60; halfwheel and Neptune list 6 1/2 x 60. Kristoff scores strength 4 out of 5; Neptune lists medium.

cigars.about: Kristoff's value priced line, introduced at the 2011 trade show and named for Glen Case's two children. A Kristania Maduro with a Brazilian wrapper followed in 2014.
cigars.researchNote: Kristoff's site lists this blend as Kristania Criollo, next to Kristania Maduro. Kristoff scores strength 3 out of 5 and Neptune lists medium; Holt's lists medium-full.

cigars.about: Kristoff's older mild blend with a Honduran grown shade wrapper over Dominican and Nicaraguan tobacco. It is no longer in Kristoff's own lineup.
cigars.researchNote: Halfwheel reports that retailers say the blend was renamed Kristoff Shade Grown in 2019; Kristoff did not confirm this. Neptune is the only source found for the mild rating. The line name is spelled Brittania.

cigars.about: An Ecuadorian Habano wrapped La Aroma de Cuba that debuted in 2008, the year production moved to My Father Cigars. It was Cigar Aficionado's number 4 cigar of 2008.
cigars.researchNote: Ashton reworked the blend in 2020 to be a little stronger and added the 6 x 60. The maker rates it medium-full; Neptune and Famous list it as medium.

cigars.about: A fuller San Andrés Oscuro wrapped La Aroma de Cuba introduced in 2012, using a top priming wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler. Most sizes are lightly box pressed.
cigars.researchNote: Launched as Mi Amor Reserva and renamed La Aroma de Cuba Reserva in 2022. Some retailers still list it under the old name. The 6 1/2 x 60 Pomposo is the round, non-pressed size.

cigars.about: The mildest La Aroma de Cuba, released in 2023 with an Ecuadorian grown Connecticut-seed wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler from the Garcia family's farms.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates it mild-medium; Neptune lists it as medium. Halfwheel's reviewer found plenty of pepper but little nicotine strength.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Nicaraguan Habano, shade grown in Namanji
cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro released in 2021, made entirely from Garcia family tobacco with a shade grown wrapper from their Namanji farm. All six sizes are box pressed.
cigars.researchNote: The wrapper is shade grown but dark, not a light Connecticut type leaf. The maker rates it medium-full; Neptune lists it as medium.

cigars.about: La Aurora's 107th anniversary blend from 2010, built on a sun grown Ecuadorian wrapper over Dominican binder and a mixed filler. It starts mild and builds to medium-full, and became one of the company's core lines.
cigars.researchNote: The maker now sells it as 107 Ecuador; the band just reads 107. Halfwheel lists the wrapper as Ecuadorian Sumatra (Habano sun grown in 2010) and adds Brazilian filler. The maker's chart prints the Lancero at 6 1/8 x 40; halfwheel lists 6 7/8 x 40. Some U.S. retailers list the Robusto at 4 1/2 x 50 and the strength as medium.

cigars.about: The first Nicaraguan puro from La Aurora, blended by Manuel Inoa and rolled in the Dominican Republic. It is the Nicaragua entry in the 107 Tobaccos of the World series.
cigars.researchNote: All Nicaraguan tobacco but rolled in the Dominican Republic. The maker's chart shows the Toro at 5 1/2 x 54 and Churchill at 7 x 47; halfwheel lists 5 3/4 x 54 and 7 x 50. Only Robusto, Toro and Gran Toro launched in the U.S. Strength is disputed: the maker's gauge reads 85/100 and Neptune says full; Famous Smoke and halfwheel say medium.

cigars.about: The third blend in La Aurora's value-priced Time Capsule (Original Blends) series, launched in 2017. The name honors 1903, the year the company was founded and says it first worked with Cameroon wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: The maker says the wrapper is now Cameroon seed grown in Ecuador; halfwheel, Cigar Aficionado and retailers list it simply as Cameroon. The U.S. launch had four sizes (Robusto, Toro, Churchill, Gran Toro); the maker's chart adds Belicoso, Cetros, Corona and tubed versions.

cigars.about: One of the two original Time Capsule (Original Blends) cigars from 2016, wrapped in Dominican-grown corojo. The year marks when La Aurora says it began blending with corojo wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's text describes the strength as medium to strong, but its own gauge reads 60/100 and Famous Smoke and Neptune list it as medium. At the 2016 launch the Churchill was 7 x 50 and the Toro 5 1/2 x 54; the maker now lists 7 x 47 and 5 3/4 x 54.

cigars.about: The Connecticut-wrapped member of La Aurora's Time Capsule (Original Blends) series, launched in 2016 alongside the 1962 Corojo. The year marks when La Aurora says it began blending with Connecticut wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: The maker lists an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper, Ecuadorian binder and Peruvian leaf in the filler. Halfwheel, Cigar Aficionado and retailers list a Dominican binder with Dominican and Nicaraguan filler, and Neptune calls the wrapper U.S. Connecticut Shade. Retailers split between mild and medium.

cigars.about: The fourth Time Capsule (Original Blends) cigar, released in 2019 with a Brazilian maduro wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler. It is the fullest of the series and priced as an everyday smoke.
cigars.researchNote: Early descriptions, still used by some retailers, list Dominican binder and Dominican and Nicaraguan filler; the distributor corrected it to all Nicaraguan. The maker's chart shows the Toro at 5 1/2 x 54 and adds a 41 ring Cetros; halfwheel lists the Toro at 5 3/4 x 54.

cigars.about: The Connecticut-wrapped version of Preferidos, La Aurora's top line, best known for its tubed double figurado. It is the mildest of the Preferidos blends.
cigars.researchNote: The maker now brands Preferidos as the 1903 Edition and calls this blend Connecticut on the straight sizes. The maker's chart lists the Toro at 5 3/4 x 54; halfwheel and Famous Smoke list 5 1/2 x 54.

cigars.about: The Brazilian maduro version of Preferidos, La Aurora's top line, best known for its tubed double figurado. Straight sizes were added in 2017.
cigars.researchNote: The maker now brands Preferidos as the 1903 Edition and calls this blend Maduro on the straight sizes. The maker's chart lists the Toro at 5 3/4 x 54; halfwheel and Famous Smoke list 5 1/2 x 54.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Cibao Valley), Brazil, Nicaragua, Peru
cigars.about: The Ecuadorian Sumatra version of Preferidos, La Aurora's top line, best known for its tubed double figurado. The maker describes it as earthy, spicy and medium bodied.
cigars.researchNote: The maker now brands Preferidos as the 1903 Edition and calls this blend Ecuador on the straight sizes. The maker's chart lists the Toro at 5 3/4 x 54; Famous Smoke lists 5 1/2 x 54.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Cibao Valley and andullo), Pennsylvania (USA), Nicaragua
cigars.about: A La Aurora line built around andullo, a traditional Dominican tobacco that is cured pressed inside palm-pod rolls instead of in piles. A full leaf of andullo goes into the filler of each cigar; the name means Dominican DNA.
cigars.researchNote: Not a Dominican puro: the binder is Cameroon and the filler includes Pennsylvania and Nicaraguan leaf. The wrapper's seed type is not published. Famous Smoke lists it as full in its specs and medium-full in its description; halfwheel's reviewer found it medium.

cigars.about: The regular-production cigar marking 115 years since La Aurora's founding in 1903. It pairs an Ecuadorian wrapper with a Brazilian binder and Dominican, Nicaraguan and Brazilian filler.
cigars.researchNote: Sold in the U.S. as the 115th Anniversary. This is the regular line; a separate limited edition (announced 2018, in the U.S. in 2019) used a Dominican corojo wrapper and reached the U.S. only as a Belicoso and Gran Toro. The maker and halfwheel say only that the wrapper is Ecuadorian; Famous Smoke calls it Habano.

cigars.about: The second line from Tony Bellatto's La Barba, released in 2014 and blended with help from Robert Caldwell and Henderson Ventura. It was dropped in 2022 after a fire destroyed the factory that made it.
cigars.researchNote: Discontinued in October 2022 after the Tabacalera William Ventura fire, so only leftover stock remains. A 6 x 54 Toro was part of the launch and was dropped in 2016.

cigars.about: La Barba's first maduro blend, released in 2018 by Tony Bellatto with a Mexican San Andrés wrapper over an Indonesian binder. It grew into a small family with later Mexi-Sol and Shade versions.
cigars.researchNote: Announced as Primitivo and renamed before shipping over a trademark conflict. The original orange-band blend is also called Ricochet Crü Oscuro. Neptune calls it medium; halfwheel's review found medium-full strength building to full. After the 2022 fire at Tabacalera William Ventura, production moved to the Ventura family's El Maestro factory.

cigars.about: A Dominican cigar with a sun grown Nicaraguan Habano wrapper over binder and filler from La Flor Dominicana's own farm. It first came out in 2006 as Coronado by La Flor, was dropped in 2013, and returned in 2015 under the La Flor Dominicana name.
cigars.researchNote: Originally sold as Coronado by La Flor from 2006, discontinued in late 2013 and relaunched in 2015 with the same blend. It placed number 2 on Cigar Aficionado's Top 25 for 2006. Strength is Holt's rating; the maker only says rich in body.

cigars.about: A dark-wrapped La Flor Dominicana blend that mixes Dominican and Nicaraguan filler, sold in 50-count cabinets. It arrived in 2011 and comes back in limited runs because the wrapper is hard to source.
cigars.researchNote: Wrapper sources disagree. The maker and Neptune say Nicaraguan Habano; halfwheel's 2011 review and 2015 news listed an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper with a Dominican Sumatra binder. Halfwheel's reviewer found it below the brand's usual strength.

cigars.about: La Flor Dominicana's Cameroon-wrapped line, using dark, oily, aged upper-priming Cameroon leaf over Dominican and Nicaraguan tobacco. The maker describes it as smooth but full bodied and keeps supply small.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls the line very limited because of the wrapper, while Famous Smoke says it is now regular production. The box-pressed No. 3 was the 2000 Series No. 3 until it was moved into this line in 2014.

cigars.about: La Flor Dominicana's Connecticut-wrapped line, dating to 1997 and best known for the short, bulging El Jocko perfecto. It is milder than the rest of the brand but has more punch than most Connecticut cigars.
cigars.researchNote: The El Jocko perfecto tapers from 32 to 54 ring and also comes in a Maduro with a Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper. Holt's and halfwheel call the line medium; Famous Smoke describes it as medium to full bodied.

cigars.about: La Flor Dominicana's mildest line and a descendant of the company's very first cigar from 1994. It was rebuilt in 2025 with new blends and red and gold packaging, in a Natural and a Grand Maduro version.
cigars.researchNote: Blend shown is the 2025 relaunch Natural. The old Suave had an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper, and the maker's site and some retailers still describe it. Grand Maduro uses a San Andrés wrapper and Jalapa binder. Halfwheel found the new Natural mild in strength with a fuller body; Neptune lists it as medium.

cigars.about: A dark La Flor Dominicana blend whose name is Latin for the night, sold in a round black box. It was blended by Tony Gomez, Litto's son, and came out in 2015.
cigars.researchNote: Holt's and Famous Smoke list it as full, but halfwheel's reviewer put body and strength closer to medium-plus.

cigars.about: A San Andrés-wrapped blend released in 2014 to mark La Flor Dominicana's 20th anniversary and named for the year the company was founded. The sizes are named after dances.
cigars.researchNote: The Tango size was added in 2015. A limited 6 x 54 version was also sold inside a commemorative beer stein.

cigars.about: A Churchill with a pigtail cap from La Flor Dominicana, named after a step in the tango as a nod to Litto Gomez growing up in Uruguay. It pairs a San Andrés maduro wrapper with an Ecuadorian Corojo binder.
cigars.researchNote: Essentially a one-size line: the 7 x 48 Churchill. A small Petite version followed in 2020; halfwheel lists it at 4 1/4 x 32 and Neptune at 4 1/8 x 34.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: Dominican (grown on the maker's La Canela farm)
cigars.about: Litto Gomez's namesake Dominican puro, made only from tobacco grown on La Flor Dominicana's own farm in La Canela, wrapper included, and released by vintage year. It was introduced in 2003.
cigars.researchNote: Sold from 2003 to 2015. A planned return has not happened as a full line, though a TAA-only Emeraude toro (6 x 54) shipped in late 2024. Sizes are from the 2015 release. The wrapper seed is not published. The maker gives no strength; halfwheel's reviews put it at medium-full, and Neptune lists the related Small Batch as full.

cigars.about: La Flor Dominicana's first candela, a green-wrapped cigar with an Ecuadorian wrapper, Nicaraguan binder and Dominican filler from the company's farm. It is medium bodied but has more punch than most candelas.
cigars.researchNote: Double Claro is another name for a candela, the green wrapper. The sizes are named for their ring gauge.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Piloto Cubano, Criollo 98, Pelo de Oro)
cigars.about: One of the two original La Galera blends from Jochy Blanco's Tabacalera Palma, launched in early 2016. It puts an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper over Dominican tobacco Blanco grows himself, at a modest price.
cigars.researchNote: Strength ratings differ: Neptune lists mild and calls it mild to medium bodied, Famous Smoke lists medium, and halfwheel's reviewer found very little strength. La Galera means the rolling room, and the sizes are named for things found in one.

cigars.filler: Dominican Republic (Piloto Cubano, Criollo 98, Pelo de Oro)
cigars.about: One of the two original La Galera blends from Jochy Blanco's Tabacalera Palma, launched in early 2016. It shares its Dominican binder and filler with the Connecticut but uses an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper for more spice.
cigars.researchNote: Famous Smoke and Neptune both list medium strength, though Famous Smoke's description calls the smoke medium-full. Same binder and filler as La Galera Connecticut; only the wrapper differs.

cigars.about: The maduro member of the La Galera family from Jochy Blanco's Tabacalera Palma, added in 2016. A Mexican San Andrés wrapper covers Dominican piloto cubano and criollo 98 from Blanco's own farms.
cigars.researchNote: Retailers split on strength: Famous Smoke lists full, while Neptune lists medium strength and describes it as full bodied. Halfwheel gives the Cortador as 6 1/4 x 52; both retailers list 6 1/8.

cigars.about: A box-pressed La Galera blend from Jochy Blanco, named for the year his family's Tabacalera Palma was founded and released in 2016 for the factory's 80th anniversary. It uses an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper over Dominican tobacco from Blanco's La Canela farms.
cigars.researchNote: Famous Smoke's spec line says Connecticut Shade, but its own description, Neptune and halfwheel all give Ecuadorian Habano. Famous Smoke says it came out in 2017; halfwheel covered the launch at the 2016 trade show. Both retailers rate it medium and describe it as medium to full bodied.

cigars.about: A darker, bolder companion to Serie R, with a very dark Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler. It came out in 2010 and is no longer on the maker's list.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune lists Dominican Republic and full strength; Holt's lists Nicaragua, a Nicaraguan wrapper and medium-full. General Cigar said in 2013 that no La Gloria Cubana had been made in Nicaragua before then, which supports Dominican Republic. A fourth size, Rojo (6 1/2 inches), also existed but its ring gauge could not be confirmed.

cigars.about: A La Gloria Cubana blend created by Michael Giannini, with an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper, a Connecticut Habano binder and extra ligero from the Dominican Republic and Nicaragua in the filler.
cigars.researchNote: Not on the maker's current list. Famous Smoke still sells it; Neptune shows it as no longer available. Both list it as full strength, though Famous also describes the blend as medium-bodied. Neptune lists the No. 13 at 5 1/2 x 54.

cigars.about: A La Gloria Cubana made at the STG Esteli factory in Nicaragua and named for that city. It pairs a Nicaraguan Jalapa wrapper with Honduran binder and filler, so it is not a Nicaraguan puro.
cigars.researchNote: Not the same as Serie R Esteli, which is a separate, older blend.

cigars.filler: Brazil (Mata Fina), Dominican Republic (Olor, Piloto Cubano), Nicaragua (Jalapa)
cigars.about: A box-pressed La Gloria Cubana named for the Spanish press method, where cigars go into divided trays right after rolling to set their shape. The blend uses tobacco from four countries under a Nicaraguan Jalapa wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: The maker describes it as medium-bodied; Famous Smoke lists it as full.

cigars.about: A limited edition shaped by votes from more than 2,000 members of the La Gloria Cubana Society, the brand's online fan group. The first release in 2022 was a Honduran puro; a second, different blend followed in 2023.
cigars.researchNote: Blend shown is the 2022 release (2,500 boxes of 20). The 2023 Society Cigar II is a different blend: Honduran Habano wrapper, Ecuadorian Sumatra binder, Dominican and Nicaraguan filler, with earth, leather, hazelnut and coffee notes.

cigars.about: A La Gloria Cubana made by Ernesto Perez-Carrillo Jr., whose family owned the brand until 1999, at his own factory in the Dominican Republic. Each cigar carries a second band with his name.
cigars.researchNote: Made at Perez-Carrillo's factory, not at General Cigar Dominicana like most La Gloria Cubana lines.

cigars.about: A La Gloria Cubana made exclusively for Famous Smoke Shop, introduced at the store's Cigarnival event in 2013. It wraps Nicaraguan filler and a Honduran binder in a dark Ecuadorian Sumatra Oscuro leaf.
cigars.researchNote: Famous Smoke Shop exclusive. Sizes are the ones Famous sells now; the 2013 launch sizes were different (5 x 52, 6 x 54, 6 1/8 x 60, 7 x 52). Famous lists it as medium, though it launched as a stronger take on the regular line.

cigars.about: La Palina's everyday, value-priced line. The original 2012 Classic had a Brazilian wrapper and was made at PDR Cigars; since the 2017 revamp the base blend is sold as Classic Natural with a Honduran wrapper, alongside Connecticut, Maduro and Rosado versions.
cigars.researchNote: Now sold as Classic Natural. Blend shown is the maker's listing; halfwheel reports a Honduran binder and adds Honduran filler, and lists the Robusto at 5 1/2 x 50. First reported as made at General Cigar Dominicana, later at STG Danli in Honduras.

cigars.about: The Connecticut shade version of La Palina's value-priced Classic line, introduced with the 2017 revamp. An Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper covers a Dominican binder and Dominican and Nicaraguan filler.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune lists strength as medium and describes it as mild to medium-bodied. First reported as made at General Cigar Dominicana; halfwheel later reported the Classic lines are made at STG Danli in Honduras.

cigars.about: The maduro version of La Palina's value-priced Classic line, with a dark Honduran wrapper and binder over Dominican, Nicaraguan and Honduran filler.
cigars.researchNote: This is the 2017 blend. An earlier La Palina Maduro from 2012 had a Mexican wrapper and is a different cigar. First reported as made at General Cigar Dominicana; halfwheel later reported the Classic lines are made at STG Danli in Honduras.

cigars.about: The dark, full-strength member of La Palina's Label Series, launched in 2014. The maker says it is loaded with Central American ligero.
cigars.researchNote: Sources disagree on the blend and where it is made. The maker lists Habano Maduro over Nicaraguan binder and filler. The 2014 original was made at PDR Cigars in the Dominican Republic with a Brazilian wrapper. Neptune still shows the Brazilian blend but names Honduras and Plasencia, and lists the Gordo at 6 x 58.

cigars.about: A member of La Palina's Label Series built for flavor instead of strength. It starts mild and creamy and settles at medium, with plenty of spice.
cigars.researchNote: Launched in 2015 from PDR Cigars in the Dominican Republic in four sizes; Neptune lists the later version as made by Plasencia in Honduras. Neptune marks every size discontinued and the maker's main product list no longer shows it. Neptune also listed a 6 x 60 Gordo.

cigars.about: A La Palina Label Series cigar that began in 2018 as a single toro for Tobacconists' Association of America shops and went nationwide in three sizes in 2019. It is made in Danli, Honduras.
cigars.researchNote: Wrapper is disputed: the maker lists Ecuador (Sumatra), halfwheel reported Ecuadorian habano in 2018 and Honduran habano in 2019, and Neptune's spec says Ecuadorian Sumatra-seed while its description says dark Habano. The maker calls it medium to full-bodied; Neptune lists medium.

cigars.about: A collaboration between La Palina and Rocky Patel, made at Plasencia's El Paraiso factory in Honduras. It started in 2017 as a single toro for Tobacconists' Association of America shops and became a regular line in 2018.
cigars.researchNote: Wrapper is disputed: the maker lists Ecuador (Habano), while halfwheel and Neptune list a Honduran wrapper. halfwheel listed the Robusto at 5 1/2 x 50; the maker and Neptune list 5 x 50. A 4 x 54 Bullet was a limited size. Each cigar is aged at least six months in cedar rooms.

cigars.about: A limited series named for founder Sam Paley's wife, Goldie Drell, and rolled at El Titan de Bronze in Miami's Little Havana. The blend includes medio tiempo leaf, each cigar has a fan-tail cap, and new sizes come out in small runs.
cigars.researchNote: Every size is a limited run in boxes of 10, usually one or two new releases a year. Until she retired in 2017 every Goldie was rolled by Maria Sierra, who once rolled Cohibas in Havana. Sizes are from halfwheel's release list; the maker's page gives different measurements for two of them.

cigars.about: La Palina's early everyday cigar; the name is Spanish for 'the daily'. It was made in Honduras with a Honduran corojo wrapper, a double Honduran binder and Nicaraguan filler, and the small KB (Kill Bill) size began as part of this line.
cigars.researchNote: Not on the maker's product list and no longer sold at Neptune, but halfwheel still named an El Diario series in a March 2023 La Palina price notice. The same blend is sold as the KB Series. Neptune's spec says medium and its description says medium to full; the maker called the KB size full bodied. Other sizes existed but were not confirmed.

cigars.about: The dark-wrapper half of La Palina's two Nicaragua lines. It is a Nicaraguan puro with a habano oscuro wrapper, medium to full in body.
cigars.researchNote: Reblended in 2023 when production moved to Joya de Nicaragua. The 2016 original was made by AJ Fernandez with an Ecuadorian oscuro wrapper.

cigars.about: The light-wrapper half of La Palina's two Nicaragua lines. It is a Nicaraguan puro with a Connecticut-seed wrapper grown in Nicaragua, light to medium in body and creamy.
cigars.researchNote: Reblended in 2023 when production moved to Joya de Nicaragua. The 2016 original was made by AJ Fernandez with an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper, and Neptune's listing still describes that version and calls it medium.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan cigar named for Luciano Meirelles, the blender behind Luciano Cigars (formerly ACE Prime). It started in 2020 as a single lancero and became a regular line with three thicker sizes in 2022.
cigars.researchNote: The maker lists the wrapper as Ecuadorian Habano Corojo 99; some early coverage called it Ecuadorian Sumatra. The maker lists the Belicoso as 5 x 50, while halfwheel listed it as 5 1/2 x 52 when it launched in 2022. The brand was sold under ACE Prime until 2022.

cigars.about: A medium-strength blend from Luciano Meirelles whose Latin name means "let there be light." It pairs a high-priming Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper with all-Nicaraguan binder and filler.
cigars.researchNote: Originally rolled in Nicaragua at Tabacalera Pichardo under the ACE Prime name. Production moved to Plasencia's Tabacos de Oriente in Danli, Honduras, with those cigars shipping from late 2024; the maker says the blend did not change.

cigars.about: A four-size line from Luciano Cigars, developed by Luciano Meirelles with sales manager Mike Dounoulis and retailer Frank Cossio of Astorian Cigar Co. It uses a double binder and filler from three countries and reached stores in April 2023.
cigars.researchNote: The maker gives no strength rating. Halfwheel's review of the Rothschild called it mild for most of the cigar, rising to medium at the end. Famous Smoke's spec table says Full while its description says medium-bodied.

cigars.about: The dark-wrapper version of the classic Macanudo, finished in Connecticut Broadleaf. It stays on the mellow side for a maduro.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls it mellow to medium; Famous Smoke lists it as Medium.

cigars.about: A medium-bodied Macanudo with an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper over a Dominican binder and filler from three countries. The maker cites a 91 rating from Cigar Aficionado.
cigars.researchNote: Famous Smoke describes the binder as Brazilian Mata Fina; the maker lists a Dominican La Vega Especial binder with the Brazilian leaf in the filler.

cigars.about: The first Inspirado, sold only in Europe and Canada from 2014 before reaching U.S. shops in 2016. It is made in Honduras with a Honduran wrapper and binder.
cigars.researchNote: Strength is described differently: the maker says Medium, halfwheel called it medium-full and Famous Smoke lists Full. Famous Smoke also lists the Dominican Republic as origin, but the maker and halfwheel say it is made in Honduras.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan-made Inspirado released in 2018 for Macanudo's 50th anniversary. It uses filler tobaccos aged five, ten and twelve years under an Ecuadorian Habano ligero wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Unlike most Macanudos, it is rolled in Nicaragua rather than the Dominican Republic. Halfwheel listed all three launch sizes as box pressed.

cigars.about: An Inspirado built around South American tobacco, with a Brazilian Arapiraca wrapper and Colombian filler. It reached stores in 2020.

cigars.filler: Brazil (Mata Fina), Nicaragua (Jalapa), Dominican Republic (Piloto Cubano, Cubita from Mao)
cigars.wrapperLeaf: Connecticut Shade grown in Bahia, Brazil
cigars.about: A limited Inspirado wrapped in Connecticut-seed shade tobacco grown in Bahia, Brazil, which is an unusual place to grow that leaf. It came out in 2021 and returned in 2024.
cigars.researchNote: Limited edition: 2,000 boxes of Toro and 1,500 of Churchill in 2021, then a second run in 2024. The maker's page also shows a 6 1/4 x 52 Torpedo.

cigars.about: A 2019 take on the Macanudo Café blend that swaps the U.S. Connecticut Shade wrapper for Ecuadorian Connecticut and adds Nicaraguan filler. General Cigar described it as creamy and medium-bodied.
cigars.researchNote: It no longer appears on the maker's website, so it may be out of production. Check stock before promising it.

cigars.about: Macanudo Vintage is a series of cigars built around a wrapper crop from one standout year. The current Connecticut Shade edition is Vintage 2010, whose wrapper was aged for about a decade.
cigars.researchNote: Vintage is a series, and each year's edition is its own blend. Details here are for Vintage 2010, which shipped in 2021. The maker also sells Vintage Maduro 2013 with a Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper. The maker calls Vintage 2010 mellow to medium; Famous Smoke lists Medium.

cigars.about: A coffee-infused cigar and the first flavored Macanudo, launched in 2018 for the brand's 50th anniversary. It is hand rolled with an Indonesian wrapper, a Philippine binder and Nicaraguan filler.
cigars.researchNote: This is a flavored (infused) cigar. It launched simply as M by Macanudo; the maker now calls it M by Macanudo Coffee since other flavors have joined the family.

cigars.about: A darker, fuller Macanudo named for the year the brand started. It debuted in August 2008 as a break from the mellow Café style.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates it medium to full; Famous Smoke lists it as Medium.

cigars.about: A full-strength Man O' War blend made by AJ Fernandez in Esteli, Nicaragua, using high-priming ligero filler under an oily Ecuadorian Habano wrapper. Man O' War is a Cigars International brand.
cigars.researchNote: Famous Smoke lists it as Full, while Blind Man's Puff reviewers rated it medium-strong.

cigars.about: The mild member of the Man O' War family, made by AJ Fernandez with an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper over Nicaraguan tobacco. A small amount of ligero in the filler keeps some of the brand's character.
cigars.researchNote: Man O' War is a Cigars International brand, so most shops will not carry it. Blend and sizes here come from one retailer, CigarPlace, whose table lists a Nicaraguan binder while its write-up says the cigar is bound in Ecuadorian Connecticut.

cigars.about: A small, strong Nicaraguan puro that AJ Fernandez is said to have first blended for himself. It is a 5 x 42 corona with a pigtail cap and unfinished foot.
cigars.researchNote: Sold in two wrappers: a natural Nicaraguan Habano and a Habano Maduro. Blind Man's Puff rated the Maduro medium-strong rather than full.

cigars.about: The top-of-the-line Man O' War, made by AJ Fernandez in small yearly batches with a dark Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper over Nicaraguan ligero. It costs well above the rest of the brand.
cigars.researchNote: Strength is described inconsistently: CigarPlace's spec table says Medium while its write-up calls it full-bodied, and Bespoke Unit rates the body medium to full. Bespoke Unit describes the wrapper as Sumatra Maduro and says about 10,000 are made a year.

cigars.about: The second Matilde line, built to be bolder than Renacer, with a dark Mexican San Andres wrapper. It is the strongest of the company's core blends.
cigars.researchNote: The maker's current site lists a Dominican binder; its earlier site, halfwheel and Neptune all say Ecuadorian Sumatra. The maker rated it Full; halfwheel's review found medium-full and Neptune lists Medium. Launched at Tabacalera Matilde, then moved to Tabacalera Palma in December 2015.

cigars.about: Matilde's third line, a sharply box-pressed blend made to sit between Renacer and Oscura in strength. Every size is box-pressed.
cigars.researchNote: Wrapper disagrees: the maker's current site says Ecuadorian Sumatra, but its earlier site, halfwheel and Neptune all say Ecuadorian Habano. The maker rated it Medium-Full and halfwheel's review agreed; Neptune lists Medium.

cigars.about: The mildest cigar in the Matilde range, a Dominican-made blend under an Ecuadorian Connecticut shade wrapper. A San Andres wrapped Serena Maduro was added in 2023.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates it Mild-Medium and calls it the mildest in its range; Neptune lists Medium. The Robusto was 5 1/4 x 54 at launch and the maker now lists it at 50 ring. Serena Maduro is a separate blend.

cigars.about: Matilde's series of small-batch limited releases, made at Tabacalera La Isla in Santiago rather than the factory that makes the core lines. Three numbered blends have come out so far, each with its own wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: A series, not one blend. No. 1 (2021): Mexican San Andres wrapper. No. 2 (2022): Ecuadorian wrapper, corojo per halfwheel, Sumatra per the maker's site. No. 3 (2026): Ecuadorian wrapper, Habano per the maker. Halfwheel lists all-Dominican filler for No. 1 and No. 2; the maker lists Dominican and Nicaraguan for all three.

cigars.about: One of the two lines Mel Shah launched MBombay with in 2014, made in Costa Rica with long-aged tobaccos from five countries. It is the mild, creamy Connecticut blend in the range.
cigars.researchNote: Halfwheel's 2018 Torpedo review lists an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper and Ecuadorian binder, against the line's name and the 2014 launch report. Halfwheel also gives Corona 5 x 43, Robusto 4 1/2 x 48 and Perfecto 6 x 50. The brand was dormant from 2020 to 2024 and Classic is not on the maker's current menu.

cigars.about: A 2015 MBombay line made in Costa Rica, blended to sit between the brand's Connecticut Classic and Corojo Oscuro. It is a medium Ecuadorian Habano blend with Nicaraguan and Peruvian filler.
cigars.researchNote: Halfwheel's launch report gives the Corona as 5 x 43 and the Robusto as 4 1/2 x 48; the maker's site lists 5 1/2 x 43 and 4 1/2 x 50. The brand was dormant from 2020 to 2024 and Habano is not on the maker's current menu.

cigars.about: A box-pressed MBombay line from Mel Shah, made in Costa Rica and notable for using Paraguayan and Peruvian tobacco in the filler. It was built for lots of flavor without heavy strength.
cigars.researchNote: The wrapper is a hybrid of Connecticut Desflorado and Mejorado 2004 seed grown in Ecuador, so it is not a plain Connecticut shade. A separate Gaaja Maduro uses a Brazilian Mata Fina wrapper. Pronounced GUY-yuh.

cigars.about: A limited production MBombay line made in Costa Rica, named for the Sanskrit word for peacock. The 2014 original used a Dominican corojo wrapper, and it came back in 2026 as an aged release with a different blend.
cigars.researchNote: Fields show the 2014 blend; halfwheel lists its binder as Peru, and gives the Lancero as 7 x 38, Toro 6 x 52 and Salomon 7 x 58. The 2026 Mora (rolled 2019) is a different blend: Mexican San Andres wrapper, Ecuadorian binder, Honduran, Nicaraguan and Pennsylvania filler, in Robusto and Toro only.

cigars.about: A maduro line named for the Micallef Ambassadors, the brand's fan club, who helped pick the name. It is made at Micallef's own factory in Esteli.
cigars.researchNote: The maker and Neptune call the wrapper Nicaraguan Maduro; halfwheel lists it as Nicaraguan Sumatra. The 4 x 46 size is sold as the lowercase Micallef a. Halfwheel calls the 6 3/4 x 54 a toro extra.

cigars.about: The first cigar in Micallef's Color Series, made as the brand's strongest blend after its fan club asked for something bolder. It is a low-priced San Andres maduro rolled at the company's factory in Esteli.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates it Full; halfwheel's review found it closer to medium-full. A 3 1/2 x 50 Firecracker has also been made.

cigars.about: The third cigar in Micallef's Color Series, after Black and Blue, sold in the same two sizes at the same prices. It pairs a Mexican San Andres Habano wrapper with a broadleaf binder.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates it Full; Neptune lists it as Medium. The wrapper is Habano seed grown in San Andres, Mexico.

cigars.about: The second cigar in Micallef's Color Series, a medium follow-up to the stronger Black. It is made at the company's factory in Esteli and sold in a Robusto and a Toro.
cigars.researchNote: The wrapper is Sumatra seed grown in San Andres, Mexico, and it is a light natural brown, not a dark maduro.

cigars.about: The Habano-wrapped half of Micallef's Herencia pair, a medium Nicaraguan blend. Herencia means heritage and the line is presented as the Gomez-Sanchez family's heritage cigar.
cigars.researchNote: Shares its binder and filler with Herencia Maduro; only the wrapper differs.

cigars.about: The maduro-wrapped half of Micallef's Herencia pair, with the same binder and filler as Herencia Habano under a darker Nicaraguan wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: The maker and halfwheel list a Nicaraguan maduro wrapper; Neptune lists a Pennsylvania wrapper. The maker's site spells the line Herencia Madura.

cigars.about: The mildest blend in the Micallef range, named after Reata, the restaurant Al Micallef owns in Fort Worth, Texas. It was designed as an after-dinner cigar.
cigars.researchNote: The wrapper is Sumatra seed grown in San Andres, Mexico, and it is light in color, not a maduro. The maker rates it Mild to Medium; Neptune lists Mild. The maker's current size list leaves out the Churchill and Torpedo, and Neptune lists the Torpedo at 6 1/8 inches.

cigars.about: Named for Migdalia Sanchez, the Cuban-born matriarch of the Gomez-Sanchez family that runs Micallef's factory. The wrapper, binder and filler are all aged about four years.
cigars.researchNote: The maker rates it Medium to Full; Neptune lists Medium. It started as a single 4 x 46 size, with the Toro and Corona Extra added in 2019. The 5 x 40 Special Edition honors International Women's Day.

cigars.about: A Micallef blend credited to the Gomez-Sanchez family's master cigar maker, Don Pedro Gomez. The line started with mostly figurado shapes, and a Robusto and Toro were added in 2023.
cigars.researchNote: Some retailers list it as Gomez Sanchez Leyenda. The maker rates it Medium to Full; Neptune lists Full. The 7 1/2 x 54 No. 1 comes in a coffin.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: The Nicaragua Series is a Nicaraguan puro made for Montecristo by A.J. Fernandez at his factory in Esteli. It joined the brand's core lineup in 2018 as a bolder alternative to the Dominican-made lines.
cigars.researchNote: The maker only says the wrapper is Nicaraguan; Famous describes it as a Habano Rosado from Jalapa. Famous and Holt's list it as medium-full, Neptune as medium, Mike's as full. Famous says it is rolled at Plasencia, but the maker and halfwheel both say A.J. Fernandez's factory in Esteli.

cigars.about: Monte by Montecristo is a Dominican-made line with an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper and a double binder of Dominican Olor and Nicaraguan Corojo over aged Dominican filler. Altadis U.S.A. launched it in 2013 as a stronger, more affordable Montecristo.
cigars.researchNote: Retailers disagree on strength: Mike's says medium, Famous medium-full, Neptune full. Not shown in the maker's current Montecristo lineup, though retailers still list it. The AJ Fernandez version is a different, Nicaraguan-made blend.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A box-pressed follow-up to Monte by Montecristo, made in Nicaragua by A.J. Fernandez for Altadis U.S.A. It pairs an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper with a Nicaraguan Corojo 98 binder and Nicaraguan and Dominican fillers.
cigars.researchNote: Strength is from halfwheel's review, which found it medium-plus early and close to full by the end. Released as regular production in 2017 but not shown in the maker's current lineup, so it may be out of production.

cigars.factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
cigars.about: A heavily box-pressed Montecristo made in Esteli by A.J. Fernandez, with an Ecuadorian Sumatra Oscuro wrapper, a Mexican San Andrés binder and Honduran and Nicaraguan fillers. It was the first Montecristo made by Fernandez.
cigars.researchNote: Launched December 2016 as an exclusive for JR Cigar and its distributor Santa Clara. Neptune and Mike's list it as full; halfwheel's review found it closer to medium-plus.

cigars.about: An extension of the Montecristo White Series that swaps the Ecuadorian wrapper for a 2008 vintage Connecticut Shade leaf grown on Altadis U.S.A.'s own farms in the Connecticut River Valley. Peruvian tobacco is added to the Dominican and Nicaraguan filler.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune lists it as mild and Holt's as medium; halfwheel's review found it mild at the start and medium by the end. Not shown in the maker's current lineup and sold out at Holt's, so availability may be limited.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro made for Montecristo by the Plasencia family as an offshoot of the Epic line. Its name refers to curing the tobaccos in small piles so the wrapper, binder and filler flavors blend together.
cigars.researchNote: A different blend and factory from the Dominican-made Epic. Strength is from halfwheel's review. Shipped December 2017 as regular production but not shown in the maker's current lineup, so it may be out of production.

cigars.about: A Dominican-made Montecristo honoring tobacco grower Jose "Pepe" Mendez, whose family revived the Cuban-seed Pilotico tobacco used in the blend. It comes in boxes styled like vintage trunk luggage.
cigars.researchNote: Some retailers list it as Pepe Mendez Pilotico. Released as regular production in 2016 but not shown in the maker's current lineup, so it may be out of production.

cigars.about: The first release in the Montecristo Volume Series, made in Honduras for distributor Santa Clara Inc. and blended by Altadis U.S.A.'s Grupo de Maestros. After rolling, the cigars rest 100 days in cedar bins, and the boxes are made to look like the Dumas novel.
cigars.researchNote: An exclusive for Santa Clara Inc., the distributor tied to JR Cigar, so it is not in Altadis's regular lineup. Tobaccos are said to be aged up to 10 years. Volume 2: The Rendezvous is a different blend.

cigars.about: A series of limited Montecristo releases blended by members of Altadis U.S.A.'s Grupo de Maestros, with one buncher and one roller chosen to make every cigar in a release. The series began in 2016.
cigars.researchNote: Each batch is a different blend. The blend and size here are Batch 1 (2016, re-released in 2018 as a TAA exclusive of 50,000 cigars). Artisan Series III (2018) is an all-Dominican 6 1/4 x 52 belicoso limited to 2,000 boxes of 25.

cigars.about: A limited Montecristo released in 2019 to mark the 50th anniversary of Tabacalera de García, the Dominican factory where it is made. It uses an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper over a Dominican binder and Dominican and Nicaraguan fillers.
cigars.researchNote: The 50 is for the factory, not the brand. The Toro was limited to 8,000 boxes of 10; the No. 2 was sold only in 75 Elie Bleu humidors of 100 cigars. In 2021 JR Cigar got its own round 6 x 50 torpedo in the same blend, the Cincuenta JR 50th, limited to 500 boxes of 10.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan-made Montecristo produced at the Plasencia factory and credited to Nestor Plasencia. The blend draws on tobaccos from Nicaragua's main growing regions under a Habano Rosado wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: Confirmed only at Famous Smoke Shop; the maker's site does not list it and no launch year is published. Famous's spec sheet says medium while its description says medium-full. Filler regions named are Jalapa, Esteli and Condega.

cigars.about: The core line of the brand, created by Jaime Garcia as a tribute to his father Jose "Pepin" Garcia. It pairs an Ecuadorian Habano Rosado wrapper with tobacco from the family's farms in Esteli.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls this line simply My Father; shops often add Original. It is not the Don Pepin Garcia Original (Blue Label). Famous describes the wrapper as a Habano Rosado and Criollo hybrid.

cigars.about: The lighter member of the My Father family, blended by Pepin and Jaime Garcia with an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper over Nicaraguan tobacco from their own farms. It keeps some of the house spice in a milder format.
cigars.researchNote: Strength listings disagree: Famous says mild-medium and the launch announcement called it mild, while Holt's lists medium-full.

cigars.about: A My Father line with an oily Ecuadorian Habano Rosado wrapper over Cuban-seed tobacco from the Garcia farms. The name means The Great Offering and the artwork follows a cigar brand of the same name from around 1913.
cigars.researchNote: The maker calls it a medium to 3/4 cigar. Famous lists medium and halfwheel found it just above medium, while Holt's lists medium-full.

cigars.about: A My Father line named for the promise Jose "Pepin" Garcia made to his family before leaving Cuba, that he would prove himself in the cigar world. It has a dark Ecuadorian wrapper over Nicaraguan tobacco from the family farms.
cigars.researchNote: Strength varies by source: Holt's says medium-full, Famous says full, halfwheel found medium-plus. The maker's spec line says Nicaragua Habano for the wrapper, but its own description, halfwheel and retailers all say Ecuadorian.

cigars.about: A Connecticut Broadleaf cigar made as a tribute to Janny Garcia; the name means the female owner. It was blended by Pete Johnson of Tatuaje with Jaime Garcia and is distributed by My Father Cigars.
cigars.researchNote: Sold under its own name. It was meant to be lighter than most My Father cigars: the maker says medium to full body, but halfwheel and Holt's both found it medium. The No. 13 comes in boxes of 12, the rest in boxes of 21.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro from the Garcia family that began as Don Pepin Garcia's first limited edition and later returned as a regular line. The current version uses a sun grown Criollo 98 wrapper.
cigars.researchNote: First sold in 2007 as a limited edition of 850 boxes per size; brought back in 2013 as a regular line with a different blend. The maker rates it 3/4 to full; Famous and Holt's list it as full.

cigars.wrapperLeaf: H-2K-CT hybrid, a sun grown Cuban-seed leaf grown in Connecticut
cigars.about: An extension of El Centurion built around a Cuban-seed wrapper grown in Connecticut, over Nicaraguan binder and filler grown by the Garcias. The sizes are box-pressed.
cigars.researchNote: The wrapper is a sun grown Cuban-seed leaf raised in Connecticut, not a Connecticut Shade leaf. The maker says medium to full bodied; Famous says medium to medium-full and Holt's lists medium.

cigars.about: A dark Connecticut Broadleaf cigar blended entirely by Jaime Garcia, son of Don Pepin Garcia. It debuted in one size at a New York City event in December 2009 and then joined regular production.
cigars.researchNote: The maker says medium to full bodied and halfwheel found medium-full, while Famous and Holt's call it full. A Figurado (48/52 ring) was added in 2023; the maker lists it at 5 5/8 inches, halfwheel at 5. There is also a separate Connecticut-wrapped version.

cigars.about: A value-priced Nicaraguan puro from My Father Cigars made with short filler in the Cuban sandwich style. The maker describes it as its first short-filler house brand, sold in green cabinet boxes of 20.
cigars.researchNote: This is a short-filler (Cuban sandwich) cigar, not long filler like the rest of the My Father range. Sold under the Tabacos Baez name. No source checked gives the release year.

cigars.about: The darker version of Flor de las Antillas, with an Ecuadorian Habano Oscuro wrapper over Nicaraguan tobacco from the Garcia farms. It is lightly box-pressed and carries a second band to set it apart from the original.
cigars.researchNote: First sold in April 2015 as a Federal Cigar store exclusive; it became a national regular line in late 2016. The maduro wrapper is Ecuadorian Habano, not broadleaf.

cigars.about: A high-priced My Father cigar, named for the Garcia family and sold in boxes of 10 at select retailers only. The blend uses aged tobaccos including the rare Pelo de Oro leaf.
cigars.researchNote: Limited production rather than a one-time edition, about $35 a cigar. The maker rates it 3/4 to full and halfwheel found medium-full; Holt's lists full. A 5 3/4 x 52 Robusto Deluxe was a 2021 limited release of 3,000 boxes.

cigars.about: The first My Father cigar made in Honduras, rolled at the family's new factory in El Paraiso with Honduran binder and filler from their Finca La Opulencia farm. All four sizes are box-pressed and the blue packaging nods to the Honduran flag.
cigars.researchNote: Made in Honduras, not Nicaragua like the rest of the My Father range. Famous lists strength as medium; Holt's lists medium-full. halfwheel lists the Robusto at 54 ring; the maker and retailers say 52.

cigars.about: The line named for Miami Cigar & Co. co-founder Nestor Miranda, first released in 2006 and brought back in 2019 after a five year absence. The current Habano version is a Nicaraguan puro made at My Father Cigars in Estelí.
cigars.researchNote: Two blends today: the Habano (described here, also sold as Rosado) and a Connecticut with an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper that returned in 2022. Strength varies by source: Neptune says medium, Mike's Cigars medium to full, and halfwheel's reviewer found it close to full.

cigars.about: A Nicaraguan puro with a corojo wrapper, added in 2016 as the fourth blend in the Nestor Miranda Collection from Miami Cigar & Co. It is made at My Father Cigars and wears the yellow-trimmed band.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune lists it as medium; Cigar Coop's review had it building to medium-full. Miami Cigar's current site shows only the Special Selection under Nestor Miranda, so the Collection may no longer be in production.

cigars.about: The Connecticut Broadleaf maduro in the Nestor Miranda Collection, the 2014 line from Miami Cigar & Co. that replaced the Special Selection. It is made at My Father Cigars and wears the red band.
cigars.researchNote: Filler sources disagree: halfwheel reports Brazil, Honduras and Nicaragua; Neptune and Cigar Coop list Dominican Republic, Nicaragua and Peru. Neptune rates it full, Cigar Coop medium to medium-full. No longer shown on Miami Cigar's site, so it may be out of production.

cigars.about: The Connecticut shade blend in the Nestor Miranda Collection from Miami Cigar & Co., made at My Father Cigars. It is the 2012 Special Selection Connecticut blend renamed in 2014, and it wears the blue band.
cigars.researchNote: Neptune's spec says medium but its description calls it mild bodied, and it omits Honduras from the filler. The Special Selection Connecticut name came back in 2022 with a close but not identical blend, and Miami Cigar's site now lists only that version.

cigars.about: One of the original Nub blends from Oliva, a short and very thick cigar built to hit its sweet spot from the first puff. This version pairs an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper with Nicaraguan filler for a creamy smoke.
cigars.researchNote: Oliva's Nub site lists a Cameroon binder; Holt's and Neptune list a Nicaraguan binder. The launch year is given as 2007 on the Nub site's Connecticut page and by Holt's, but 2008 on the Nub site's story page and by halfwheel.

cigars.about: One of the original Nub blends from Oliva, a short and very thick cigar meant to deliver full flavor from the first draw and still last about an hour. It uses an Ecuadorian habano wrapper over Nicaraguan long filler.
cigars.researchNote: Oliva's Nub site lists an Indonesian binder; Neptune and Mike's Cigars list Nicaraguan. Retailers disagree on strength: Holt's says medium, Mike's medium to full, Neptune full.

cigars.about: The dark-wrapped member of Oliva's core Nub range, in the brand's short and very thick format. It is known for roasted coffee and dark chocolate notes over Nicaraguan filler.
cigars.researchNote: Wrapper sources disagree: Oliva's Nub site lists Mexico, while Holt's, Neptune and Mike's Cigars all describe a Brazilian maduro wrapper. The blend may have changed over time, so do not promise a guest one or the other.

cigars.about: A core Nub blend from Oliva that wraps Nicaraguan binder and filler in an African Cameroon leaf, in the brand's short and very thick format. It is known as the smooth, naturally sweet one of the range.
A Sumatra-wrapped Nub from Oliva in the brand's 4 x 60 format. It is not part of the core range shown on the Nub site.
cigars.researchNote: Not listed on Oliva's Nub site. Cigars Direct shows a Sumatra wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler, sold in boxes of 10, with strength shown as both full and medium-full. Treat the blend and strength as unconfirmed.

cigars.about: A coffee-infused cigar in Oliva's Nub Nuance line, the macchiato-style middle of the three roasts. It has a Sumatra wrapper over Dominican tobacco and is made for Oliva in the Dominican Republic.
cigars.researchNote: This is a flavored cigar, launched in 2014 as Nub Cafe Macchiato and renamed under Nub Nuance from 2016. It is made in the Dominican Republic by General Cigar, not at Oliva's factory. Mike's Cigars lists a Nicaraguan binder with Dominican and Nicaraguan filler, unlike the Nub site.

cigars.about: A Nub from Oliva's Studio Tobac group that puts two Brazilian maduro wrapper leaves over Nicaraguan filler in the brand's short, thick format. Dub is short for double maduro.
